citations.claim: N shows green at first violating step with 0s all-red clearance
E shows yellow one step before the abrupt switch to NS green

counterfactual.change: Removed the single emergency event on S at t=123; otherwise identical. Without preemption the cycle runs EW green/yellow/all-red normally and no rule is violated.

explanation: Emergency preemption on S at t=123 forces an immediate switch from EW green to NS green: EW yellow lasts only 1s (needs 6s) and the all-red clearance is skipped entirely (0s vs required 2s), so NS turns green while EW has not cleared. Removing the emergency removes the failure.

violation.detail: approach 0 turned green after only 0 s of all-red (need 2 s)

vision_note: Steps 121-122 show one axis holding green while the cross axis is held at red. In step 123 those greens flip to yellow for only one frame before step 124 already shows green on the cross axis, so the switch occurs with no all-red clearance gap.
